subject: chemistry
title: Chlorine, disproportionation and water treatment
key_idea: In disproportionation, one element is both oxidised and reduced. Chlorine disproportionates in water to give HClO and ClO⁻, which kill bacteria. With cold dilute alkali it gives bleach, and with hot alkali it gives chlorate(V).

blocks.text: Chlorine can be oxidised and reduced in the same reaction. This section covers what disproportionation is and the oxidation numbers of chlorine.

items.meaning: A reaction in which the same element is both oxidised and reduced.
The ion ClO⁻, with chlorine at +1. Hypochlorite is the older name.
The ion ClO₃⁻, with chlorine at +5.

blocks.text: In each case below, chlorine at 0 goes both up and down in oxidation number.

items: Disproportionation is oxidation and reduction of the same element.
In chlorine reactions, Cl at 0 forms Cl⁻ (reduced) and ClO⁻ or ClO₃⁻ (oxidised).

sections.heading: Chlorine with water, and water treatment

blocks.text: Chlorine dissolves in water and reacts with it. This section covers the reaction, what kills bacteria, and the benefits and risks.

blocks.label: Chlorine with water
where: HClO: chloric(I) acid, the main disinfectant

items: Chlorine is oxidised from 0 to +1 in HClO and reduced from 0 to −1 in Cl⁻.
HClO ionises a little: HClO ⇌ H⁺ + ClO⁻.
HClO and ClO⁻ are the active species that **kill bacteria**.
In sunlight, chlorine and water can also form chloride ions and oxygen.
**Benefit**: chlorine kills bacteria and prevents diseases such as cholera and typhoid.
**Risk**: chlorine gas is toxic and must be stored and handled carefully.
**Risk**: chlorine can react with organic matter in water to form chlorinated hydrocarbons, which may be harmful.
Society weighs the benefits against the risks. The benefit to health is judged to outweigh the toxic effects.
Chlorine in water makes HClO and ClO⁻, which kill bacteria.
The reaction is a disproportionation.
The benefit of safe drinking water outweighs the risks, which are managed.

blocks.text: The products depend on temperature. This section covers the two reactions with aqueous sodium hydroxide and their uses.

items: Cold, dilute NaOH gives a solution of sodium chlorate(I). This is **bleach**, used to kill germs and remove colour.
Hot NaOH gives sodium chlorate(V), which is more oxidised.
Bromine reacts in the same way. Bromine with cold NaOH gives NaBr and NaBrO.

diagram.alt: A predictor. Pick the conditions to see the products of chlorine or bromine with sodium hydroxide or water and the oxidation numbers.
A sorting activity. Decide which reactions are disproportionation.

items: Cold dilute NaOH gives chlorate(I) (bleach). Hot NaOH gives chlorate(V).
The same element is oxidised and reduced in both reactions.

checks.q: Write the equation for the reaction of chlorine with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide, and name the use of the solution.
checks.a: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O. The solution is used as bleach, to kill germs or remove colour.

checks.q: Explain, using oxidation numbers, why the reaction of chlorine with water is a disproportionation.
checks.a: Chlorine goes from 0 in Cl₂ to −1 in HCl, which is reduction, and from 0 to +1 in HClO, which is oxidation. The same element is both oxidised and reduced.

checks.q: Give one benefit and one risk of adding chlorine to drinking water.
checks.a: Benefit: it kills bacteria that cause disease. Risk: it can form chlorinated hydrocarbons, which may be harmful, or chlorine gas is toxic.

blocks.text: This part covers weighing up the decision to chlorinate water.

items: The decision balances the benefit of killing bacteria against the risk from chlorine gas and from chlorinated hydrocarbons.
Ethics matter: people have a right to choose what is in their water.
Other ways to purify drinking water include ozone and ultraviolet light. Each has its own costs, benefits and risks.
Analogous reactions use bromine in place of chlorine, with the same oxidation number changes.

blocks.text: This part covers the oxidation of metals by the halogens, and hot alkali.

items: Halogens oxidise Group 1 and 2 metals: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl and Ca + Br₂ → CaBr₂.
The halogen goes from 0 to −1, so it is reduced. The metal is oxidised, from 0 to +1 or +2.
Chlorine with hot alkali is also a disproportionation, and gives chlorate(V) as above.

blocks.text: This part covers the uses of the chlorine solutions.

items: Chlorine in water treatment is used to disinfect drinking water and swimming pools.
The solution of NaCl and NaClO from cold dilute NaOH is used as household bleach and disinfectant.
In sunlight, chlorine and water form chloride ions and oxygen: 2Cl₂ + 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + 4Cl⁻ + O₂.
